livetitle.text: MAYBE · Live system · clickable build spec

notes01.text:
Notes · 01 · Title
Hi, we're Luc and Friederike. MAYBE lets students try real work from real companies for about an hour before they choose a degree or a job. Everything you'll see is a working prototype; the companies are examples, not partners.

notes02.text:
Notes · 02 · Problem
At Stuzubi we asked students who named a dream career one question: have you actually tried it? Almost nobody had. They choose from descriptions, rankings and what their parents know. The cost of a wrong choice shows up years later.

notes03.text:
Notes · 03 · Idea
The idea: a marketplace of one-hour work trials, each branded by a company. You call AI retail buyers for Dr. Lipp, or redesign the DICE festival checkout and test it on synthetic fans. You leave with scored evidence, not a personality label.

notes04.text:
Notes · 04 · Live marketplace
This is the live marketplace. Two trials are playable today: DICE product design and Dr. Lipp sales. You can scroll and click inside the frame. The other companies are coming-soon previews.

notes05.text:
Notes · 05 · Dr. Lipp sales trial
In the Dr. Lipp trial you're a sales rep. You call three AI retail buyers by voice, handle objections about price and shelf space, and update the CRM. The black strip on top always says it's a simulated MAYBE trial.

notes06.text:
Notes · 06 · DICE design trial
In the DICE trial you're a product designer. The festival checkout loses fans; you redesign it in the editor and run it against 1,000 synthetic fans. Those results are clearly labelled as synthetic estimates, not real users.

notes07.text:
Notes · 07 · Honest scoring
Every number on MAYBE says where it came from. Rule-based checks are deterministic. Synthetic estimates come from simulated users or buyers. AI review is a model grading against a rubric you can read. And whether you closed the deal is shown on its own, never mixed into your score.

notes08.text:
Notes · 08 · Student side
After a trial, the student keeps the evidence: scores with provenance, transcripts, design files. They decide what goes into the portfolio and whether employers can see it.

notes09.text:
Notes · 09 · Employer side
Companies get a candidate board built from work they can inspect: call transcripts, design files and test results, each score linked to the rubric. From there they open the evidence and invite someone to interview.

notes10.text:
Notes · 10 · Under the hood
Under the hood: each trial is a scenario with a brief, tools and a rubric. Voice agents play the buyers, synthetic users test designs, and three kinds of scoring produce evidence with provenance. It's all built on one design system, shadcn with zinc and a single violet.

notes11.text:
Notes · 11 · What's next
Next: we start with parents, run pilots, then bring it to schools. What we'd love from you is in the three boxes. And if you have questions, ask our agent right here, it knows the project and can move the slides.

notes05b.text:
Notes · 05b · Live call
Now let's call a buyer for real. I'll talk to Mara, our AI retail buyer, live. Watch the orb react to my voice and her answers appear on the right.
